STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plate, looks medium-large, roughly 22-24 cm across.
b) Reference: the plate's edge runs about 1.2 to 1.3 times the length of the potato chunk spanning it; the leaf salad occupies about a third of the plate width. Taking the potato piece (~4-5 cm) against the plate, the plate is roughly 22 cm wide.
Final width: 22 cm (area about 484 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Roasted potato/aubergine-type pieces (cooked chunky vegetables, golden-brown): cover about 25% of the plate, about 120 cm2. Thickness: a pile of chunky pieces about 2 pieces high at the centre, ~2.5 cm average. Volume = 120 x 2.5 = 300 ml, x 0.6 density (chopped cooked vegetables) = 180 g.
- Single whole boiled/roasted potato piece (round, top centre): roughly 5 x 4 cm, about 40 g of food, treated as part of the same vegetable group; estimate 50 g.
- Mixed leaf salad (raw leafy greens, sits in a mound on the right): covers about 30% of plate, about 145 cm2, average thickness about 3 cm (loose leaves 3-6 cm, mound averages lower). Volume = 145 x 3 = 435 ml x 0.15 = 65 g.
- Light dressing/oil smear: about 1-2 g visible, negligible; count as 3 g.

Total weight about 180 + 50 + 65 + 3 = 298 g.

Energy estimates:
- Roasted vegetables (aubergine/potato with oil): about 120 kcal/100 g (oil absorbed).
- Potato piece: about 85 kcal/100 g.
- Mixed leaf salad: about 20 kcal/100 g.
- Dressing: about 70 kcal/100 g (light oil).
